title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page belongs to Grothendieck's study of the 'équation des lacets'. It sits in the Grothendieck–Teichmüller circle of ideas: a profinite free group (the script letter transcribed as \hat{C}, written \hat{G} on the next page; probably \hat{F} or \hat{\pi}), two automorphisms or elements \rho, \sigma (presumably of finite order, as in the braid/modular relations) and a group \Gamma_{\rho,\sigma} built from them. Several groups map onto \Gamma_{\rho,\sigma}:
- \delta_\rho : Z_\rho \to \Gamma and \delta_\sigma : Z_\sigma \to \Gamma, where Z_\rho, Z_\sigma are centralizer/normalizer-type groups;
- \delta_G : G_{\rho,\sigma} \to \Gamma, with kernel the free profinite group itself;
- \delta_B : B_{\rho,\sigma} \to \Gamma, an extension of \Gamma by L_0.

The previous page defined two groups:
- S M^0 = \{(u,a,b,U) : \delta_B(u) = \delta_\rho(a) = \delta_\sigma(b) = \delta_G(U)\};
- M^0 = \{(a,b,U) : \delta_\rho(a) = \delta_\sigma(b) = \delta_G(U)\}.
It also gave the exact sequence 1 \to L_0 \to SM^0 \to M^0 \to 1.

This page reformulates these definitions as iterated fibre products over \Gamma_{\rho,\sigma}.
- (55) S_0M^0 \simeq M^0 \times_\Gamma B. So S_0M^0 is the extension of M^0 by L_0 obtained by pulling back, along M^0 \to \Gamma, the extension B of \Gamma by L_0.
- (56) M^0 \simeq (Z_\rho \times_\Gamma Z_\sigma) \times_\Gamma G_{\rho,\sigma}; the inner factor Z_\rho \times_\Gamma Z_\sigma is labelled T.
- (57) Since \delta_\rho, \delta_\sigma, \delta_G are surjective, the diagonal map \delta^*_M : M^0 \to \Gamma is surjective. Its kernel is the product of the kernels: SZ_\rho \times SZ_\sigma \times \hat{C}, denoted M^{0+}. Here SZ_\rho = Z_\rho \cap \hat{C} = \mathrm{Cent}_{\hat{C}}(\rho), and likewise for \sigma (definitions recalled from (44)).
- (49)–(50), renumbered locally. In the same way, S_0M^0 \simeq B \times_\Gamma Z_\rho \times_\Gamma Z_\sigma \times_\Gamma G; the first three factors are labelled S_0T^0. This gives the exact sequence 1 \to L_0 \times SZ_\rho \times SZ_\sigma \times \hat{C} \to S_0M^0 \to \Gamma \to 1.
- (51) The canonical embedding \hat{C} \to M^0, u \mapsto (1,1,u), identifies \hat{C} with the third factor of the kernel.

The next page uses this to produce extensions of quotients of \Gamma by \hat{C}. It then gives a set-theoretic parametrization S_0M^0 \simeq SG_{\rho,\sigma} \times \hat{G}, via (u,a,b,U) \mapsto (ua^{-1}, ub^{-1}, uU^{-1}), on the way to the 'loop equation' unknowns \alpha, \beta, f, g, h.

Purpose: bookkeeping of the symmetry groups acting on the solution set of the loop equation, cast as fibre products and extensions.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The kernel computation is correct for fibre products of surjections over a common base: the kernel of the diagonal map is the product of the kernels. This needs ker \delta_G = \hat{C} and ker \delta_B = L_0, consistent with the previous page.
Equation numbers (49)–(57) are reused from the previous page. This is a numbering inconsistency in the manuscript, not a mathematical error. The notation also wavers between S M^0 and S_0 M^0.

ideas.what: Expressing groups of compatible tuples (u,a,b,U) as iterated fibre products over \Gamma_{\rho,\sigma}, and S_0M^0 as the pullback of the extension B along M^0 \to \Gamma
ideas.modern_name: Fibre product of groups over a common quotient; pullback of a group extension
ideas.where_published: This specific setting belongs to the unpublished 'Variations sur l'équation des lacets' notes (cote 140-3)

ideas.what: Kernel of the diagonal map from an iterated fibre product of surjections equals the product of the kernels (SZ_\rho \times SZ_\sigma \times \hat{C}, and with L_0)
ideas.modern_name: Exact sequences for fibre products of epimorphisms

ideas.what: Centralizers of \rho, \sigma in the profinite free group (SZ_\rho = \mathrm{Cent}_{\hat{C}}(\rho)) as components of the symmetry group of loop-equation solutions
ideas.modern_name: Centralizers in profinite free groups / GT-type automorphism groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld, Ihara (GT setting); Grothendieck (Esquisse/Longue Marche program)
ideas.where_published: The general theme appears in Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche; these particular groups do not, as far as known

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine structural bookkeeping: fibre products and exact sequences over \Gamma_{\rho,\sigma}. It is part of a larger unpublished computation, but this page contains no new result or connection on its own.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 probably reads 'On a aussi, dans l'interprétation précédente' or similar.

Lines 3–5 read roughly: '& S_0M^0_{\rho,\sigma} s'exprime à l'aide de M^0_{\rho,\sigma} et B_{\rho,\sigma}, et on trouve que c'est l'extension de M^0_{\rho,\sigma} par L_0 qui est l'image inverse de l'extension B_{\rho,\sigma} de \Gamma_{\rho,\sigma} par L_0. Et on a'.
In (55)–(57), \Gamma_{\rho,\sigma} is written as a script \Gamma/\gamma with indices \rho,\sigma, and the fibre products are over it.
The symbol rendered \hat{\mathbb{C}} is a script letter (probably the profinite free group, written \hat{G}/\hat{F} elsewhere), not the complex numbers.
The underbrace in (56) is labelled T^0_{\rho,\sigma} (partly blotted), and in (49) it is labelled S_0T^0_{\rho,\sigma}.
After (57): 'où on a posé (44)', with 'posé' partly struck.
In (57) the arrow M^0 \to \Gamma is labelled \delta^*_M, and the kernel is defined as M^{0+}_{\rho,\sigma} ('déf =').
In (51) the map is labelled i_{\hat{C}}.
